claim_being_bridged: That a Rigvedic lemma Turner marks with a Dravidian arrow records contact between Indo-Aryan and Dravidian speakers.
tested_here: Partly. The lemma's presence and its stratum are measured (DE-M-009 to DE-M-012); the etymology is Turner's, not this record's.
notes: A dictionary's attribution and a historical contact event are two things. Turner's bracket is a judgement made in the 1960s, resting in 36% of cases on Burrow and in 38% on Mayrhofer (DE-M-030). To cross this bridge the etymologies must be checked individually against DEDR and against Indo-Aryan-internal alternatives - the null, HYP-E-000. That work is not done here.

claim_being_bridged: That loan candidates clustering in Arnold's Popular stratum shows the borrowing happened late in the Rigvedic period.
tested_here: The clustering is measured: 10 of 21 tokens, against a 13.9% baseline (DE-M-012).
verdict: WEAK - THREE SEPARATE FAILURES OF INDEPENDENCE
notes: First, the strata are Arnold 1905 and nothing else (DEP-001). Second, Popular stratum and book 10 are not independent instruments (DEP-004), so a book-order confirmation would be circular. Third, a metrical stratum is a compositional layer, not a calendar. And the candidate set is 15 lemmas. The measurement stands; this inference does not follow from it without work not done here.

claim_being_bridged: That where Dravidian and Munda languages are recorded now constrains where they were three thousand years ago.
tested_here: The modern distribution is measured (DE-M-021 to DE-M-025).
notes: Constitution §4.P forbids converting modern areal distribution automatically into prehistoric substrate. The measurement is a starting point for the geography gate and never its conclusion. Brahui is the standing demonstration that the modern map understates the past distribution of at least one family - which is why HYP-E-002's geography verdict is 'adverse' and not 'fails'.

claim_being_bridged: That Dravidian or Munda speech implies a distinct ancestry, and that ancestry results speak to language.
tested_here: No. No genetic evidence was retrieved or used in this unit.
notes: Constitution §4.E: genetic admixture dates for present-day Munda-speaking populations constrain demographic models but do not directly date or exclude a language. IH-112 and IH-119 carry ancestry claims at INHERITED-UNVERIFIED and none of them is used here. This unit is lexical and geographic only.

link_from: a substrate donor in the northwest
link_to: the language of the Indus civilisation
claim_being_bridged: That establishing a Dravidian presence in the northwest supports a Dravidian reading of the Indus script.
notes: Two separate claims. HYP-E-001 passing its gate says nothing about HYP-E-008, which is deferred out of scope. The site's existing position (IH-136, IH-118) is untouched by this unit and stays INHERITED-UNVERIFIED.

claim_being_bridged: That an arrow in CDIAL means the etymology is accepted in the field today.
tested_here: Partly: hedging is counted (DE-M-005) and the cited authority is counted (DE-M-028 to DE-M-030).
notes: CDIAL was compiled 1962-66. Constitution step 11 requires current standing to be established separately, and nothing retrieved here establishes it: Mayrhofer's EWA, which Turner cites in 85 cases, was not retrieved, and neither was any post-1990 assessment. What is in the register is Turner's judgement with its date attached, and that is all it is offered as.

claim_being_bridged: That a starred Proto-Dravidian form can stand in evidence beside a Rigvedic lemma.
tested_here: The two are held in separate tables and separate registers throughout (DE-M-013 against DE-M-014).
notes: Constitution §4.E's attestation gradient. DEDR offers no reconstructions at all, which is why distinctions 1 and 2 required separate sources here: the reflexes come from SRC-061 and the starred forms from SRC-062. Nothing in this unit lets a starred form supply attestation.

claim_being_bridged: That a word appearing only inside Rigvedic compounds counts as attested in the Rigveda.
tested_here: Yes - measured and separated into three columns (DE-M-020).
verdict: REFUSED, AND THE DISTINCTION IS PRODUCTIVE
notes: kunda and mayura have no Rigvedic simplex but do occur in compounds, and Turner says so himself. Merging the two would have added them to the simplex count; treating compound absence as total absence would have lost them. Both errors were available and both are avoided by keeping three columns. The columns are string matches and need case-by-case review: of the four raised, two are real and two (*garda to gardabha-, pota to potar-) are spelling coincidences.

claim_being_bridged: That an object of foreign material at a site shows the material was transported there.
tested_here: Yes - traced to its warrant. Damour 1865 (DRM-001).
notes: This is the one bridge in the domain that the founding inference actually licenses, and it licenses only this. Damour's rule concludes to transport of the object or of the matter it is made from. It says nothing about who carried it, in how many stages, by trade or gift or tribute or raid, or over what interval. Pollard and Liu add that in down-the-line exchange taking years or generations any demonstrated source-object link 'may not be archaeologically meaningful'.

link_from: an Indus manufacturing technique in Mesopotamia
claim_being_bridged: That beads drilled with Indus-type Ernestite drills and shaped to Indus forms, found at Kish and Ur, show Indus craftspeople resident there.
tested_here: Yes - and the source's own wording is the test. SRC-109 concludes that Indus craftspeople 'produced or taught others to make' such beads.
verdict: REFUSED AS STATED; the weaker form stands
notes: The evidence establishes an Indus technological repertoire - tools, forms, drilling technique, bleaching - operating in Mesopotamia. 'Or taught others' is the source conceding that the repertoire can travel without its originators, and once conceded it cannot be withdrawn in the conclusion. A third possibility the source does not raise is that the tools travelled as trade goods: Ernestite drill bits are small, portable, and the study reports that 'some of the tools were imported'. What stands is that the technique was present; who held it is not settled by drill-hole morphology. DRR-008 is PROVISIONAL for this reason.

link_from: a person designated by a foreign toponym
claim_being_bridged: That individuals recorded as dumu me-luh-ha in Ur III Girsu were speakers of a Meluhhan language.
tested_here: Yes - tested against the names those individuals actually bear in the same documents.
notes: The bearers carry Sumerian theophoric names - Ur-Lamma, Ur-Ig-alim (DRM-011). That does not show they spoke Sumerian at home, because a Sumerian archive records people under names its scribes could write; and the designation does not show they spoke anything else, because dumu me-luh-ha may be a patronymic on a personal name rather than an ethnicon. The designation and the name point different ways and neither settles the other. This is the domain's cleanest instance of the owner's rule: material movement, population movement and language movement are three claims, and here the second is arguable and the third is simply not in evidence.

claim_being_bridged: That Dilmun's adoption of the Indus weight standard shows an institutional relationship with the Indus, and beyond that a population presence.
verdict: FIRST STEP ACCEPTED AS PROVISIONAL; SECOND STEP REFUSED
notes: Metrological convergence is a fourth kind of claim and a strong one: a weight standard is an institutional convention, not a commodity, and adopting it implies sustained transactional contact in a way that possessing an object does not. That much stands, on one author's evidence (DEP-032), hence PROVISIONAL. The step to population is separate and is not carried by weights: standards are adopted by the party that wants to trade, and adoption is evidence of who was accommodating whom, not of who was living where. Note also that the standard then circulates as a pure abstraction - GIN2-DILMUN, 552 of 826 Dilmun occurrences, a unit of account (DRM-015) - which is the clearest case in the unit of something moving with no material moving at all. | CORRECTED 2026-09-09: the occurrence figure was understated by a factor of about 2.5 by a classifier fault (BF-032). The correction strengthens this row rather than weakening it - two thirds of the corpus's Dilmun occurrences are the standard rather than the place.

link_to: the descent and ethnicity of its makers
claim_being_bridged: That the Gulf Type seal's Indus-derived glyptic and its round Harappan boss show that Harappans, or their descendants, made the first ones, broke away from the Indus establishment, married into Dilmunite families, and assimilated.
tested_here: Yes - the chain is set out explicitly enough in the source to be taken apart.
notes: The first link - that the seal type is stylistically and technically derived from Indus sealing practice - is an argument about objects and is well made. Every link after it is about people, and each is an addition: 'Harappans or acculturated Harappans' already concedes that the craft can be held by non-Harappans; 'must at least periodically have resided' is an inference from seasonal trade; the breakaway group, the strategic marriages and the rapid assimilation are a narrative constructed to explain why no other Harappan cultural traits appear. An absence of Harappan traits is being explained by a mechanism that would produce that absence, which is not the same as evidence for the mechanism. The source itself notes the Indus script in the west was 'rapidly adjusted to accommodate writing in a language other than that of the Harappans', which is a fifth claim again - a script moving without its language.

claim_being_bridged: That establishing where a stone formed establishes who supplied it.
tested_here: Yes - against the two cases in this unit where the two are separately attested.
verdict: REFUSED, AND THE TWO ARE SEPARATELY ATTESTED
notes: DSf names Sogdiana as the region lapis was brought from; Sar-e Sang lies in Bactria (DRB-013). Dilmun 'served only as a trading post; it was never the ultimate place of origin of any of the traded products' (DRM-016). A source is a geological fact, an exporter is a political and commercial one, and the object register keeps them in different columns because the record itself does. The exporter column is NOT ESTABLISHED for 13 of 13 objects in this unit.

claim_being_bridged: That where an object was found indicates where it was made.
tested_here: Yes - against the Gonur vessel and the Kish necklace.
notes: An Umm an-Nar type vessel at Gonur Depe has a findspot in Central Asia and a manufacturing tradition in south-east Arabia (DRB-016). Within one Kish necklace, beads of one geological source carry two different workshop standards (DRR-007). Findspot, workshop and manufacturing tradition are three of the owner's ten fields and this unit found no object where all three coincide and are independently established.

link_from: a commodity label in a text
claim_being_bridged: That a textual term translated 'carnelian' or 'lapis lazuli' names that mineral.
notes: The term rendered 'red-stones' is equated with carnelian by most scholars but 'could also refer to red jaspers or garnets' (DRR-011). In the corpus, 844 of 1,552 occurrences of za-gin3 carry no stone determinative and may be a colour or quality term (DRB-019), and 257 matches of gug are a baked good or a plant (DRR-013). A commodity label is a category in someone's administrative language, and the English mineral name is a modern translator's choice. Under the translation standard the choice must not be allowed to decide the historical question.

claim_being_bridged: That an object catalogued as lapis lazuli or carnelian is lapis lazuli or carnelian.
tested_here: Yes - against a case where analysis overturned an attribution.
notes: Beads at Konar Sandal identified as calcite from the artefacts' appearance are gypsum alabaster (DRM-005). Of 796 objects in the museum-candidate register, 0 carry an analysis, and the catalogue has no column in which one could be cited (DRM-021). The register's column is therefore named cdli_material_attribution. This is the owner's first trap in its museum form: not every blue object in a case labelled lapis is lapis.
